$comment: Which of this suite's own tests checks which specification clause.
The CONF-* clauses in spec/11-conformance.md constrain a conformance SUITE rather than an
implementation, so they cannot be checked by a test vector -- a vector is data handed to an
implementation, and there is no input that demonstrates 'the scorer imports nothing'. They
are checked by this suite's own tests, which are code.
This file is how tools/lint_normative.py sees them. It is not a list of promises: the linter
verifies that every test named here actually exists in test_conformance.py, so a renamed or
deleted test breaks the build rather than silently leaving a clause unchecked.
Adding a clause here is a claim that the named tests really do check it. That claim is on the
person adding it, which is why each entry names specific tests rather than the file.
